alt_text: album cover of Elvis Presley's RCA Victor record featuring a black-and-white photograph of him singing while holding an acoustic guitar; large red vertical text spells "ELVIS" on the left, green bold text reads "PRESLEY" across the bottom, with the label logo and "New Orthophonic High Fidelity Recording" text in the top right corner.
album cover of: A person wearing a nurse’s cap and blue gloves, a white coat with a "blink-182" name tag over a red top; a colorful butterfly tattoo is visible on their left arm.

album cover of: A woman stands in front of rows of hanging blue garments, holding up a bright blue dress on a wooden hanger with both hands, wearing a white top and dark pants. The background features various shades of blue clothing items on racks.

album cover of: A close-up photograph shows hand-drawn Japanese kanji in bold black ink against a textured beige paper background, with irregular brush strokes and small ink splatters creating an informal artistic style.

album cover of a musical release features a photograph of a German Shepherd barking in the upper left corner over an abstract background with green and beige brushstrokes; below the dog is a grid of small circles, with decorative curved lines partially overlapping the landscape.

Album cover of Grace Jones’s *Island Life* features a woman balancing on one leg against a light blue wall with wooden flooring. She wears an orange top, red knee bandage, holds a microphone in her right hand while grasping her left foot, and stands on a small blue mat.

album cover of Green Day’s "Dookie" features a vibrant, cartoon-style illustration with a chaotic urban scene centered around a large yellow starburst explosion emitting red smoke from a jet aircraft flying through the sky. The background includes numerous characters, buildings, and floating elements like a hot air balloon labeled "BAD YEAR" and missiles marked "DOOKIE," along with the title prominently displayed in bold red lettering at the bottom.

album cover of HUM's "You'd Prefer an Astronaut" featuring a black-and-white zebra standing against a solid green background with "HUM" and the album title in white text at the top left, and "45:53" at the bottom right.
album cover of: A woman with long blonde hair kneels on a grassy hillside wearing a flowing white gown, set against a backdrop of dense trees shrouded in mist under an overcast sky.

album cover of The Strokes' "Is This It" features a high-contrast black-and-white photograph showing a glossy black leather glove resting on the upper back of a nude person. The band name appears in black text at the top left, while "IS THIS IT" has "IS" highlighted in red above the rest of the title.

album cover of: A surreal digital illustration featuring multiple nude children with blonde hair navigating a landscape of weathered stacked stones under an orange sky, where circular holes are visible in some rock formations and vibrant green, yellow, and orange coloration dominates the scene.

album cover of The Smiths features a vertical green "THE SMITHS" text alongside a black-and-white 2x2 collage showing four images of a person wearing a helmet with "MEAT IS MURDER" printed on it and carrying equipment against a wooded background.

album cover of The Smashing Pumpkins' *Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness* features a vintage-style illustration of a woman in historical clothing seated on a large yellow star against a dark blue cosmic background with planets, stars, and nebulae; ornate white text displays the band name and album title at the top left.

album cover of: Nirvana's 'Nevermind' features an underwater scene with a baby reaching toward a one-dollar bill suspended by a fishing line, and the text "NIRVANA NEVERMIND" displayed in the lower left corner.
album cover of: A nighttime parking lot scene featuring a red sedan parked on asphalt covered in fallen leaves, surrounded by trees and a distant vehicle visible under dim lighting.

album cover of N.W.A.'s "Straight Outta Compton" features five men looking down in a circle with one holding a firearm; large red text at the top reads "N.W.A." and a Parental Advisory sticker for explicit content appears on the left.

album cover of Beck's "Odelay" featuring a grassy field with distant trees and a white jump obstacle with black-and-white striped bars in the foreground; a large textured hay-like structure arcs above the obstacle, overlaid with bold red text spelling "BECK! ODELAY".

album cover of a digitally distorted winter scene with bare trees rendered in vibrant blue and purple tones, a lone figure standing on a paved pathway, and intense white glare obscuring portions of the visual elements.

album cover of *Purple Rain* by Prince and The Revolution features Prince in a purple suit seated on a motorcycle with flames and smoke effects; a woman stands on a house porch staircase behind him, framed by vibrant floral patterns along the left and right edges.

album cover of Roxy Music featuring a person reclining on a bed with light-colored sheets. The individual wears a pastel blue and pink ruffled outfit with satin accents, including puffed sleeves and halter straps, while "Roxy Music" appears in cursive text at the top left.

album cover of: Fleetwood Mac’s 'Rumours' featuring a black-and-white photograph on a beige background with two figures; a man stands with one hand on his hip holding a woman’s hand, while she stands on a small stool wearing a dress with flowing sleeves. The band name and album title are displayed in stylized text at the top right.

album cover of The Beatles' Sgt Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band features a dense collage of numerous historical and fictional figures arranged in multiple rows, with the band members prominently displayed in colorful military-style uniforms; the album title "Sgt Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band" is spelled out using vibrant floral arrangements at the bottom, surrounded by various plants and decorative elements.

album cover of West Virginia Snake Handler Revival features a man with a beard wearing a white dress shirt, black suspenders, and patterned tie holding a snake against a dark wooden backdrop, with the title text prominently displayed in red at the top left and the subtitle "They Shall Take Up Serpents" below it.

album cover of Bruce Springsteen's "Born in the U.S.A." depicts a person from the waist down wearing blue jeans with a red cap tucked into the back pocket, a white tank top, and a studded belt, against a background of alternating horizontal red and white stripes resembling the American flag.

album cover of 'we will be wherever the fires are lit' by Tashi Dorji features a 3x3 grid of photographic images on a red-to-black gradient background, showcasing environmental scenes such as forests, smoke, a discarded glove, waterways, urban landscapes, and littered ground.
album cover of: A painting depicting a nude woman reclining on soft pink clouds against a blue sky background; a Parental Advisory label is visible in the bottom right corner.

album cover of The Roots' "things fall apart" features a black-and-white photograph showing people running away from uniformed police during what appears to be a protest or riot, with the album title in red text at the top right and the band name in large white text above.
album cover of: A stylized yellow banana with black stains on a white background, featuring "PEEL SLOWLY AND SEE" in small uppercase letters at the top right and "Andy Warhol" written below.

album cover of Amy Winehouse’s *Back to Black* featuring her seated on a wooden chair against a dark chalkboard background with faint white writing; she wears a white polka-dot dress, red belt, and leopard-print high heels with visible arm tattoos.

Album cover of The Mothers of Invention features a retro-style illustration against a bright yellow background. A man in a dark suit has a weasel attached to his neck with speech bubbles reading "THE MOTHERS OF INVENTION," "WEASELS RIPPED MY FLESH," and "RZZZZZ!". The artwork uses bold lines, vivid colors, and comic book elements.
